blogs.title: Why Reinforcement Learning Matters for the Next Generation of Language Models
blogs.description:
RL lets language models learn from a diversity of rewards—think solving math problems or writing code—beyond what supervised pre‑training can achieve.
When models grow bigger than 100B parameters these rewards become hard to optimize safely because tiny mistakes can cascade into complete model collapse.
This post explains why modern researchers turn to specialized RL algorithms instead of brute‑force data pipelines.

blogs.title: Token‑Level Importance Ratios Go Awry in GRPO
blogs.description:
GRPO was designed to sidestep a costly value network by comparing every generated token to its older counterpart.
But while running a probability weight per token looks clever, it actually misuses importance sampling.
The result is high‑variance gradient noise that swamps long responses—leading infrastructure crash­downs.
The article walks through this pitfall using simple examples so you’ll see why token‑level weights are dangerous.

blogs.title: Sequence Leverage Wins Back!: Introducing Group Sequence Policy Optimization
blogs.description:
GSPI flips the script—importance weights are computed on entire responses instead of single tokens.
By normalizing across response length your weights stay close together and you clip whole sequences.
The mathematics stays grounded in classic importance sampling while the intuition stays clear.
We’ll break down how this change eliminates runaway gradients and gives stable updates even when Gemini tables expand.

blogs.title: A Breakthrough for Mixture‑of‑Experts Design — No More Routing Replay Needed
blogs.description:
MoE models activate different expert weights per example.
Under GRPO that leads to wildly fluctuating per‑token probabilities (“expert‐activation volatility”) which desynchronizes old vs new policy data.
Routing Replay was a cumbersome hack forcing retries.”
GSPI’s sequence‐level approach ignores per‑token differences and treats every sample the same.
The result is smooth MoE learning without extra memory budgets—a game changer illustrated in Qwen3 results.

blogs.title: Simplicity Rules™ : How GSPI Simplifies RL Infrastructure
blogs.description:
Training engines normally recompute old policy likelihoods precisely—costly stuff especially under GPU‑cluster constraints.
Because GSPI only needs overall response scores its likelihood calculations tolerate lower numeric precision granted by inference engines.
You can now feed an SGLang vLLM forward pass directly into the policy update step—no extra passes, less bandwidth stress, even perfect fit with multi‑turn partial rollouts.
